
From the Grok social signals, PRIME stands out as a strong fit — it applies preference-based reward modeling specifically to autonomous LLM agents with empirical evaluation. The arXiv RSS signal AEM (Adaptive Entropy Modulation for Multi-Turn Agentic RL) is relevant to agentic RL but lacks clear human feedback components from the title alone. Reward Hacking in LLM-Powered Agents is a good fit thematically but the social evidence link appears unreliable. Only PRIME clears the bar with high confidence.

## Suggestions

- [PRIME: Preference Rewards with Item Matching Embeddings for Aligning LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01718) — Preference-based reward modeling method using item-matching embeddings to align autonomous LLM agents, with empirical evaluation on agentic benchmarks.
  Section: Research Papers > Reward Modeling & Preference Learning | Criteria: Applies preference learning and reward modeling in an agentic/autonomous setting, Goal-directed agent behavior shaped by learned reward models from preference comparisons, Iterative alignment loop via preference reward signals refining agent policy, Empirical outcome on agentic task benchmarks
